mainTopic: The ban on חימוץ for מנחת נסכים and לחם הפנים, the holiness of measuring vessels, and the ban on burning offering leftovers on the מזבח or its כבש
overview: The ברייתא taught that ״אשר תקריבו״ adds one more offering to the ban on letting a מנחה become חמץ. The גמרא challenges each opinion. Against רבי יוסי הגלילי (מנחת נסכים), it argues that oil cannot make dough rise, and ריש לקיש answers that water may be added. Against רבי עקיבא (לחם הפנים), it argues that he holds dry measures are not holy, and רבי יוחנן answers by switching the names. The גמרא then brings the ברייתא where רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן argue over which measuring vessels were anointed, and explains that their dispute is about the word ״אותם״. רב פפא and אביי discuss the kneading bowl, and the גמרא explains why a holy עשרון would never be swapped for an ordinary one. Then a new ברייתא learns from ״ממנו״ that leftovers of offerings may not be burned on the מזבח, and רב ששת explains how שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are included. Finally, רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue whether bringing such leftovers onto the כבש alone makes a person liable.

steps.title: Fruit juices do not make dough rise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge to רבי יוסי הגלילי: מנחת נסכים is kneaded with oil, and fruit juices do not cause leavening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And fruit juices do not cause dough to become חמץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against רבי יוסי הגלילי. How can a פסוק be needed to forbid מנחת נסכים from becoming חמץ, if it could never become חמץ in the first place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this line, the גמרא noted that מנחת נסכים is mixed with oil. Oil counts as מי פירות (fruit juice), and fruit juice alone does not make dough rise. So it seems there is nothing for the פסוק to forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit juices, such as oil or wine, as opposed to water
Cause dough to rise and become חמץ
Leavening; letting the dough become חמץ

phrases.english: And fruit juices do not cause leavening!
phrases.notes: This is the end of a question that started just before. The oil in מנחת נסכים counts as fruit juice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge to רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says ״אשר תקריבו״ adds מנחת נסכים to the ban on חימוץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנחת נסכים is made with oil, which is fruit juice. Fruit juice does not cause leavening, so a ban on leavening it would be pointless.

steps.title: מנחת נסכים may be kneaded with water
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a person may also knead מנחת נסכים with water, and it is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: רבי יוסי הגלילי used to say that a person may knead מנחת נסכים with water, and it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge. Water may be added to מנחת נסכים, so it really can become חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the dough has only oil in it. ריש לקיש shows that, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, water may be added and the offering stays valid. Once water is added, the dough can rise, so the פסוק is needed to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering brought together with the wine poured for an animal offering
He kneads it, mixing the flour with liquid
Valid; fit to be offered

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili used to say:
A meal offering of libations, one may knead it with water,
and it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a case the question did not consider, where the dough contains water
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought מנחת נסכים is made only with oil, so it could never become חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, water may also be added, so the offering can become חמץ and the פסוק is needed.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי עקיבא from the dry measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא. The flour for לחם הפנים is measured in a dry-measure vessel, and רבי עקיבא himself said that dry measures were not made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: לחם הפנים is measured with a dry-measure vessel. And we heard that רבי עקיבא said: the dry-measure vessel was not made holy.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to the other side of the ברייתא and challenges רבי עקיבא, who says the פסוק adds לחם הפנים to the ban on חימוץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flour for לחם הפנים is measured in a dry-measure vessel. If that vessel does not make it holy, the bread only becomes holy later, when it is placed on the שלחן after baking. While it is being kneaded it is not yet holy, so why would a פסוק be needed to forbid it from becoming חמץ?

keyTerms.meaning: The twelve loaves placed each week on the שלחן in the מקדש
A measuring vessel for dry items such as flour
Was made holy as a vessel of the מקדש, so that it makes what is put in it holy

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying לחם הפנים is not holy at all. The point is only about timing: it is not holy yet while the dough is being made, so the leavening ban seems to come too early.

phrases.english: The shewbread uses a dry measure,
and we have heard that Rabbi Akiva said:
The dry measure was not consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים מִדַּת יָבֵשׁ הִיא, וּשְׁמַעְנָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended רבי יוסי הגלילי, the גמרא now attacks the other opinion in the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's statement that ״אשר תקריבו״ adds לחם הפנים to the ban on חימוץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא holds that dry measures were not made holy. Then לחם הפנים is not holy while it is being kneaded, so there is no reason for a ban on letting it become חמץ.

steps.title: Switch the names in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי ראובן sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: the names in the ברייתא should be switched. רבי יוסי הגלילי adds לחם הפנים, and רבי עקיבא adds מנחת נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ראובן sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: this is the correct order of the teaching, and switch the names. ״אשר תקריבו״ comes to add לחם הפנים to the ban on חימוץ; these are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי. רבי עקיבא says: it comes to add מנחת נסכים to the ban on חימוץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by switching who said what in the ברייתא. Now רבי עקיבא is no longer the one who talks about לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are switched, רבי עקיבא says the פסוק adds מנחת נסכים, which has nothing to do with dry measures. So there is no contradiction with his view that dry measures were not made holy. רבי יוסי הגלילי now holds the לחם הפנים view instead.

keyTerms.meaning: The proper arrangement or correct version of a teaching
Switch it around; reverse the names
"That you shall bring", the words of the פסוק being expanded
To include; to add something to the law

steps.whyThisMatters: Switching names is a strong answer. Instead of explaining away a contradiction, the גמרא fixes who said what, and this changes how we understand both תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח רַבִּי רְאוּבֵן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Reuven sent in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
This is the correct version of the teaching,
and reverse the names:
"That you shall bring" is to include the shewbread in the prohibition of leavening,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
Rabbi Akiva says:
It is to include the meal offering of libations in the prohibition of leavening.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַבִּי רְאוּבֵן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כָּךְ הִיא הַצָּעָה שֶׁל מִשְׁנָה, וְאֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by switching the names in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names of the תנאים in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי עקיבא said the פסוק adds לחם הפנים, which clashes with his view on dry measures.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא really said the פסוק adds מנחת נסכים, and רבי יוסי הגלילי is the one who adds לחם הפנים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent with his own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן's switch fits another statement of his: רבי יוסי הגלילי and one of רבי ישמעאל's students said the same thing, and that student is רבי יאשיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. For רבי יוחנן said: רבי יוסי הגלילי and one of the students of רבי ישמעאל said the same thing. And who is he? רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's switch was not made up just to answer a question. It matches what he says elsewhere about רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the switched version, רבי יוסי הגלילי adds לחם הפנים, so he must hold that dry measures were made holy. רבי יוחנן elsewhere says that רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי יאשיה hold the same view. This shows that רבי יוחנן consistently places רבי יוסי הגלילי in that position.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning; he is being consistent with what he said elsewhere
The same thing; one and the same opinion

steps.whatToRemember: After the switch: רבי יוסי הגלילי says ״אשר תקריבו״ adds לחם הפנים, and רבי עקיבא says it adds מנחת נסכים. This fits רבי עקיבא's view that dry measures were not made holy, and it fits רבי יוחנן's other statement about רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own reasoning,
as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי וְאֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and one of the students of Rabbi Yishmael
said the same thing,
phrases.notes: Their shared view here is that dry measures were made holy. That is why רבי יוסי הגלילי can hold the לחם הפנים position.

phrases.english: And who is he? Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the switch in step 4 by showing it matches another statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן's switch of the names is consistent with his own approach
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי יאשיה said the same thing

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יאשיה says dry measures were anointed on the inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows רבי יאשיה holds dry measures are holy, at least on the inside. That fits רבי יוסי הגלילי after רבי יוחנן's switch.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "And he anointed them and sanctified them." רבי יאשיה says: the liquid measure was anointed both on the inside and on the outside. The dry measures were anointed on the inside but not on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what רבי יוחנן said in step 5, that רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי יאשיה say the same thing. Here is רבי יאשיה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה holds that dry measures were anointed on the inside, so they do make things holy. After the switch, רבי יוסי הגלילי also holds this, which is why he counts לחם הפנים, whose flour is measured in a dry measure. So the two of them agree.

keyTerms.meaning: A measuring vessel for liquids, like oil or wine
A measuring vessel for dry things, like flour
Was anointed with the anointing oil, which made it holy
On the inside / on the outside of the vessel

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And he anointed them and sanctified them."
phrases.notes: במדבר 7:1. This is about משה anointing the משכן and its vessels.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya says:
The liquid measure was anointed
both on the inside and on the outside;
the dry measures were anointed on the inside
and were not anointed on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 5's claim that רבי יאשיה agrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's switch, which makes רבי יוסי הגלילי hold that dry measures are holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יאשיה on anointing the measuring vessels

steps.title: רבי יונתן says dry measures were not anointed at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says liquid measures were anointed only on the inside, and dry measures were not anointed at all. He proves it from שתי הלחם, which become holy only after baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: the liquid measures were anointed on the inside and not on the outside. The dry measures were not anointed at all. You can know this, because they do not make things holy. The פסוק says: "From your homes you shall bring two loaves for waving, made of two tenths of fine flour, baked with leaven, as first fruits to ה'." When are they "to ה'"? Only after they are baked.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion, from רבי יונתן. He says dry measures are not holy at all, and he brings a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flour for שתי הלחם is measured in the עשרון, which is a dry measure. Yet the loaves only become "to ה'" after they are baked. So putting the flour into the dry measure did not make it holy, which shows that dry measures were never anointed.

keyTerms.meaning: At all
"You can know": this opens a proof
Make holy what is placed inside them
The two loaves brought on שבועות and waved

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says:
The liquid measures were anointed on the inside,
and were not anointed on the outside;

phrases.aramaic: מִדּוֹת יָבֵשׁ לֹא נִמְשְׁחוּ כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: the dry measures were not anointed at all.
You can know this, because they do not make things holy,
as it is written: "From your homes you shall bring
two loaves for waving
they shall be two tenths of fine flour
baked with leaven, as first fruits to ה'."
When are they "to ה'"?
After they are baked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second opinion in the same ברייתא, which disagrees with רבי יאשיה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liquid measures are holy only on the inside. Dry measures are not holy at all, as shown by שתי הלחם.

steps.title: What is the disagreement based on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what point רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the root of the disagreement between רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them quote the same פסוק, so the גמרא wants to know which word in it they read differently.

keyTerms.meaning: "About what do they disagree?": a question asking for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the dispute between the two opinions
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the פסוק each תנא reads differently

steps.title: They disagree about what the word "אֹתָם" leaves out
steps.stepSummary: Both agree that "אֹתָם" leaves something out. רבי יאשיה says it leaves out the outside of dry measures. רבי יונתן says dry measures are not holy anyway, so it leaves out the outside of liquid measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about "them". רבי יאשיה holds that "them" comes to leave out the outside of dry measures. רבי יונתן holds that a dry measure is not holy anyway, so no פסוק is needed to leave it out. The פסוק was needed to leave out the outside of the liquid measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole dispute comes from how each one reads the word "אֹתָם" in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אֹתָם" (them) narrows what was made holy. If dry measures are holy, as רבי יאשיה holds, the narrowing applies to their outside. If dry measures were never holy, as רבי יונתן holds, the narrowing must apply to something else, which is the outside of liquid measures.

keyTerms.meaning: To leave out, to exclude from the rule
Not holy, ordinary
The פסוק was needed

phrases.english: About "them".
Rabbi Yoshiya holds that "them"
comes to leave out the dry measure on the outside;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן סָבַר מִדַּת יָבֵשׁ חוֹל הוּא,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yonatan holds that a dry measure is not holy,
so no פסוק is needed to leave it out;
where the פסוק was needed to leave something out
was the liquid measure on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about what "אֹתָם" leaves out: the outside of dry measures (רבי יאשיה) or the outside of liquid measures (רבי יונתן)

steps.title: Why not also say that רבי עקיבא and רבי יונתן agree?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יונתן, like רבי עקיבא, holds that dry measures are not holy, רבי יוחנן should also have said that the two of them say the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him also say that רבי עקיבא and one of the students of רבי ישמעאל said the same thing. And who is that student? רבי יונתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן paired only רבי יוסי הגלילי with רבי יאשיה. It seems he should also have paired רבי עקיבא with רבי יונתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said that dry measures were not made holy (step 3), and רבי יונתן says the same. So the pairing should work just as well as the one in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let him also say": it seems he should have added this
The same thing
"And who is it?"

phrases.english: Let him also say that Rabbi Akiva
and one of the students of Rabbi Yishmael
said the same thing,
and who is he? Rabbi Yonatan.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא נָמֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְאֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא to question why רבי יוחנן's statement in step 5 was incomplete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא and רבי יונתן agree that dry measures are not holy, so רבי יוחנן should have paired them as well

steps.title: They disagree about liquid measures
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן did not pair them, because רבי עקיבא and רבי יונתן do not agree about liquid measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they do not agree with each other about the liquid measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא and רבי יונתן agree only partly, so רבי יוחנן could not say they "said the same thing".
steps.deeperAnalysis: About dry measures they agree, but about liquid measures they disagree. רבי עקיבא holds that liquid measures are holy both inside and outside, while רבי יונתן says they are holy only inside. To say "they said the same thing", the two must agree fully.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not the same, they do not agree
With each other

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי (after the switch) = רבי יאשיה: dry measures are holy on the inside. רבי עקיבא and רבי יונתן both say dry measures are not holy, but they are not called "the same", because they disagree about liquid measures.

phrases.english: Because they are not the same
with each other about the liquid measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא שָׁווּ בְּמִדַּת לַח לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the two opinions agree only partly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both say dry measures are not holy, רבי עקיבא and רבי יונתן hold the same view
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree about liquid measures, so they cannot be called "the same thing"

steps.title: רב פפא: The Kneading Bowl Should Make the Dough Holy
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: even if dry measures do not make things holy, the ביסא (kneading bowl) holds wet dough, so it should count as a liquid vessel and make the לחם הפנים holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But there is the kneading bowl, and that is a vessel for liquid!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks אביי about the idea from step 3 that, for the view that dry measures are not holy, the לחם הפנים becomes holy only later, on the שולחן. He points out that the dough already sat in a kneading bowl before that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet dough is a moist thing, so the bowl it is kneaded in counts as a vessel for liquids. Even those who say dry measures are not holy agree that liquid vessels were anointed and make things holy. So the dough should already become holy in the bowl, and the leavening ban would apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The kneading bowl or trough in which dough is mixed
Moist or liquid; here, a vessel used for wet items
But there is (introduces a challenge pointing to a fact)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But there is the kneading bowl,
which is a vessel for liquid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to step 3's premise about when the לחם הפנים becomes holy, if dry measures are not holy, and challenges it from the kneading bowl, a liquid vessel.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption from step 3 that, for those who hold dry measures are not holy, the לחם הפנים is not made holy until it is placed on the שולחן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The kneading bowl holds wet dough, so it is a liquid vessel. Liquid vessels make things holy, so the dough should already be holy at the kneading stage.

steps.title: אביי: The Dough Was Kneaded on a Leather Spread
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that we are dealing with a case where the dough was kneaded on a flat leather spread (קטבליא), which is not a holy vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For example, where he kneaded it on top of a leather spread.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the assumption from step 3 by limiting the case: the dough was not kneaded in a holy bowl at all, but on a flat leather mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leather spread is not a holy כלי, so nothing about it makes the dough holy. That leaves the שולחן as the first point where the bread becomes holy, as the challenge in step 3 assumed.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat leather spread or mat
For example; we are dealing with a case where
Kneaded (dough)

phrases.english: He said to him:
For example, where he kneaded it on top of a leather spread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dough must have been kneaded in a holy kneading bowl, so it should already be holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can be kneaded on a non-holy leather spread, so it does not become holy at the kneading stage.

steps.title: Then רבי יאשיה Could Have Answered רבי יונתן the Same Way
steps.stepSummary: If such a case can be imagined, then רבי יאשיה could have rejected רבי יונתן's proof from שתי הלחם by saying the flour was measured in a non-holy עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, about what רבי יונתן said to him, 'Know that it is so, since it does not make holy,' let him answer: we are dealing with a case where he measured it in a non-holy tenth-measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses אביי's style of answer to challenge something else: רבי יונתן's proof from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן proved that dry measures are not holy, since the שתי הלחם become holy only after baking. Using אביי's logic, רבי יאשיה could reply that the flour was measured in an ordinary, non-holy עשרון, and that is why it was not holy yet. Since רבי יאשיה did not say this, perhaps such an answer is not acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on the previous answer)
Know for yourself (introduces a proof)
A tenth-of-an-איפה measuring vessel, a dry measure
Non-holy, ordinary

phrases.english: If so,
that which Rabbi Yonatan said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יאשיה, the one רבי יונתן was arguing with.

phrases.english: Know that it is so, for it does not make holy,
let him say to him:
for example, where he measured it in a non-holy tenth-measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, דְּקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes אביי's answer from Step 13 and shows it seems to create a problem for the רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן debate.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reliability of אביי's kind of answer, and רבי יונתן's proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we may imagine a non-holy vessel to avoid holiness, רבי יאשיה could have answered רבי יונתן with a non-holy עשרון. He did not, which suggests this kind of answer does not work.

steps.title: The Cases Are Different: The Torah Requires the עשרון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. The Torah never required a kneading bowl, so kneading on a leather spread is fine. But the Torah requires measuring with an עשרון, so no one would skip the holy one and use an ordinary one.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? Granted, the kneading bowl: the Torah did not write that one must make a bowl to knead in, so kneading on a leather spread is no problem. But the tenth-measure: since the Torah said 'Make a tenth-measure and measure with it,' would someone leave the holy tenth-measure and measure with an ordinary one?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of Step 14 by showing that אביי's answer and the suggested answer for רבי יאשיה are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a leather spread is a normal, allowed option, because no vessel for kneading is commanded. But a holy עשרון is required for measuring, so a case of using a non-holy one is unrealistic. That is why רבי יאשיה could not answer that way, while אביי's answer still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
Granted; it makes sense regarding
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Leaves aside, abandons

steps.whatToRemember: A kneading bowl is optional, so the dough can avoid it. The עשרון is commanded, so we assume the holy one was used. Because of this, אביי's answer works and רבי יונתן's proof stands.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?
Granted, a kneading bowl:
the Merciful One did not write
that one should make a kneading bowl to knead in it;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָשׁ לַהּ עַל גַּבֵּי קַטְבֻלְיָא –
phrases.english: so when he kneads it on top of a leather spread,
we have no problem with it.
But a tenth-measure,
since the Merciful One said:
Make a tenth-measure and measure with it,
would he leave the holy tenth-measure
and measure with an ordinary tenth-measure?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by pointing out the difference between the kneading bowl and the עשרון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Imagining a non-holy vessel works equally well for the kneading bowl and for the עשרון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a vessel the Torah does not require can be skipped. A required vessel like the עשרון would not be replaced with an ordinary one.

steps.title: New ברייתא: Source for the Prohibition on Offering Up Non-Altar Sacred Foods
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks for the source that someone who offers up meat of a חטאת, אשם, קדשי קדשים, or קדשים קלים, or leftovers of the עומר, שתי הלחם, לחם הפנים, or שירי מנחות, violates a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: From where do we know that one who offers up meat of a sin offering, meat of a guilt offering, meat of the most holy offerings, offerings of lesser holiness, the leftover of the עומר, the leftover of the two loaves, the showbread, or the remainders of meal offerings, violates a prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that asks for a source. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the items listed are holy but are meant to be eaten, not burned on the מזבח. The ברייתא assumes that offering them up is forbidden by a לא תעשה, and it is looking for the פסוק that teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we learn this)? It asks for a source
For one who offers up (on the altar)
The leftover of the עומר offering, which is eaten
The remainder of meal offerings, eaten by the כהנים
A negative commandment, a prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these items are not holy. They are fully holy, but they are meant to be eaten rather than burned, and that is why offering them up is the problem.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
From where for one who offers up from the meat of a sin offering,
and from the meat of a guilt offering,
and from the meat of the most holy offerings,
and from offerings of lesser holiness,
and from the leftover of the omer,
and from the leftover of the two loaves,
and from the showbread,
and from the remainders of meal offerings,
that he violates a prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן לְמַעֲלֶה מִבְּשַׂר חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the debate about measuring vessels.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that forbids, as a לא תעשה, offering up sacred foods that are meant to be eaten.

steps.title: The source is the word 'of it' in the verse of leaven and honey
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its own question. The source is the פסוק of שאור and דבש. Its word ממנו teaches that anything with a part already given to the fire falls under בל תקטירו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'For any leaven and any honey, you shall not burn of it as a fire-offering to ה׳.' Anything that has some part of it already given to the fire is included in 'do not burn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now answers the question from Step 16: where do we learn that burning leftover meat or bread on the מזבח is forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק openly forbids only שאור and דבש. But the extra word ממנו ('of it') widens the rule. Any קרבן whose proper part already went on the fire has leftovers that may not be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven, the sourdough starter that makes dough rise
Honey, or any sweet fruit juice
Fire-offering / the fires of the מזבח
The prohibition 'do not burn' on the מזבח
'Of it', the extra word that the רבנן use to learn the rule

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"For any leaven and any honey
you shall not burn of it as a fire-offering to ה׳."
Anything that has a part of it for the fires
is included in 'do not burn.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ממנו in ויקרא 2:11 includes anything with a part already given to the fire under בל תקטירו.

steps.title: But the two loaves and the showbread have nothing burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים have no part burned on the fire, so how can the rule of 'something with a part for the fires' include them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do the two loaves and the showbread have any part for the fires? But a ברייתא teaches: the two loaves and the showbread are excluded, because no part of them goes to the fires!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's list. It quotes another ברייתא which says that nothing from שתי הלחם or לחם הפנים is burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from ממנו covers only things that have a part already given to the fire. Another ברייתא openly says that שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים have no such part. So it seems they should not be on the list at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed on the שולחן every שבת
'Are excluded', meaning they are left out of the rule

phrases.english: But the two loaves and the showbread:
does any part of them go to the fires?
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
Excluded are the two loaves and the showbread,
since no part of them goes to the fires!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list of Step 16 using the rule of Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's inclusion of שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule needs a part to go to the fire, and another ברייתא says these breads have no such part.

steps.title: Nothing from their own body is burned, yet they still count
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that nothing from the breads themselves is burned. But they are tied to something else that is burned, so they are still included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: nothing from its own body goes to the fires.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge. The other ברייתא only means that no part of the bread itself is burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources talk about different things. 'Nothing goes to the fire' means the bread's own body. But the bread is part of a larger קרבן that is burned, so it still counts as 'having a part for the fires.'

keyTerms.meaning: From its own body, from the item itself

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת does not deny the other ברייתא. Both are true: nothing of the bread itself is burned, yet it still belongs to a קרבן that has a burned part.

phrases.english: רב ששת said:
Nothing from its own body goes to the fires.
phrases.notes: He means the bread itself isn't burned, but what goes with it is: the כבשים with שתי הלחם and the frankincense with לחם הפנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the item's own body versus the larger offering it belongs to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since nothing of the breads is burned, they seemed to fall outside the ממנו rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are included, because the offering they belong to has a part on the fire, even though the bread itself has none.
steps.whatToRemember: בל תקטירו applies to leftovers of any קרבן with a part on the fire. That includes שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים, which belong to offerings with burned parts.

steps.title: Is bringing them only onto the ramp also forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: A new מחלוקת. If someone brings any of these leftover items only onto the כבש (the ramp), not onto the מזבח itself, רבי יוחנן says he is liable and רבי אלעזר says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one who brings up any of them onto the ramp: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, and רבי אלעזר says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about the same prohibition. Does putting the item on the ramp leading to the מזבח already count as a violation? This sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the case was burning on the מזבח itself. Now the question is whether the ramp is treated like the מזבח for this לא תעשה. רבי יוחנן holds that it is, and רבי אלעזר holds that it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
One who brings up an item
Liable, deserving punishment
Exempt, not punished

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who brings up any of them onto the ramp,
phrases.notes: 'Any of them' means all the items listed in the ברייתא in Step 16.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן says: he is liable,
רבי אלעזר says: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related question about the same prohibition
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רבי יוחנן holds that bringing leftovers onto the כבש makes one liable, and רבי אלעזר holds that it does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows whether the כבש counts like the מזבח itself for this prohibition, and the גמרא will now work through each side.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: the ramp counts like the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the person is liable. He brings a ברייתא that learns from the words 'they shall not go up to the מזבח' that the כבש is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, as a ברייתא teaches: The word 'the מזבח' would only teach about the מזבח itself. Where do we learn that the כבש is included? The פסוק says: 'And to the מזבח they shall not go up for acceptance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's side of the מחלוקת by giving his source from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the word 'מזבח' alone would cover only the מזבח itself. But the פסוק talks about 'going up' to the מזבח, and the כבש is the way you go up. So bringing the item onto the כבש is already forbidden, and רבי יוחנן says the person is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
From where do we know?
The פסוק teaches / says
For acceptance (as a pleasing offering)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says he is liable,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: "The altar":
I would only know this about the altar itself;
from where do we know it about the ramp?
The verse says: "And to the altar
they shall not go up for acceptance."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that bringing leftovers onto the כבש makes a person liable
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the words 'ואל המזבח לא יעלו' (ויקרא 2:12) to include the כבש

steps.title: What is רבי אלעזר's reason for exempting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר says the person is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר says he is exempt. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי אלעזר's reason. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw a ברייתא that seems to include the כבש. So we need to know how רבי אלעזר can say the person is exempt. The next step gives his reading of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt, not liable
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says he is exempt;
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר פָּטוּר, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing רבי יוחנן's source, the גמרא turns to the other side of the מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and reasoning for רבי אלעזר's ruling of exemption

steps.title: The word 'them' limits the ramp rule to first-produce offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from the word אותם that the כבש counts like the מזבח only for the 'first produce' offerings, not for other items.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says: 'שאור and honey... as an offering of first produce you may bring them.' 'Them': only for these did the פסוק include the כבש like the מזבח. For other things, it did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אלעזר's reason. The word אותם in the פסוק limits the כבש rule to the first-produce offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר agrees that the כבש can count like the מזבח. But he says the פסוק includes it only for 'them,' the first-produce offerings of שאור and honey. Meat of קדשים and leftover מנחות are 'other things,' so bringing them onto the כבש makes a person exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering of first produce
Them: a word that limits the rule to specific items
Included, extended (the verb, from ריבוי)
Other things

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the כבש counts like the מזבח for everything, so the person is liable. רבי אלעזר: the word אותם limits that to the first-produce offerings, so for other leftovers the person is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' is not the title 'רבי.' It is a verb meaning 'included' or 'extended.'

phrases.english: As the verse says: "Leaven and honey...
as an offering of first produce you may bring them."
"Them": it is only these that the verse included for you,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the first-produce offerings made of leaven or honey that the פסוק is talking about.

phrases.english: treating the ramp like the altar;
but for other things, it did not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22 by giving רבי אלעזר's reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word אותם limits the rule that the כבש counts like the מזבח to the first-produce offerings, so other leftovers brought onto the כבש do not make a person liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the root of the מחלוקת. Both sides accept that the כבש can count like the מזבח. They argue only about how far that rule reaches.
